analysis:
Only the test file QwenTensorParallelBatchDriverTests.swift changed. It adds build-ahead test scaffolding: Pair.ahead and aheadByRank (lines 54-58), the buildsAhead driver parameter (86 and 461), and Executor submitDecode/readDecode with a Submitted class and fault-injection hooks (108-149). Host.publishToken now allows a bounded native-frontier gap (212-218). The session's aheadDiscardLimit is set from aheadHeldLimit (161). The base text covers lines 1-619. The head text visible to me stops at line 497; the patch's changed range runs to 946, so the later new tests were not displayed. They are an unverified coverage gap.

No production code was changed, and this shipped no new attack surface. The production driver (QwenTensorParallelBatchDriver serveAhead, aheadHeldLimit) and the executor's submitDecode/readDecode are not in the supplied evidence. Relevant integration questions for the next pass, mostly under availability and integrity of inference (T-007, T-010, T-008): (1) With build-ahead, does the publication gap stay bounded so that tokens a client stopped or cancelled are never published after the stop is seen? The test relaxes publishToken to allow native to run ahead by aheadHeldLimit+1, which could mask a regression. (2) After a client stop, the discarded ahead-built tokens must not leak beyond what the owner saw. (3) Both ranks must keep an identical collective order. The tests use mismatched aheadByRank, presumably to check fail-closed behavior. (4) The corrupted-decision and failed submit/read hooks should confirm fail-closed behavior with no success published and no charge released. In the displayed tests, the retirement-ACK checks (Host.retired, confirmedRetirement) are unchanged, so the bilateral-drain invariant is still asserted. The test-only relaxation of the frontier check is the one thing that deserves a real production-code review. needs_deeper_review is true because the later head lines (498 onward) and the production driver were not visible.
